name: Estes
role: Aircrew aboard the helicopter in VN-0016
summary: The man looking back over his shoulder from the front seat in VN-0016. On 2026-09-12 his son pointed out that there seemed to be a name on the man's helmet, and Larry read it: "oh his last name is Estes, I was thinking his name was Lewis." He added that he thinks Estes was National Guard and was probably called up, that "Lewis must be somebody else," and that the man looking back was not the one flying: "Usually the guy looking back is not flying the plane and he was talking to me."
researchNotes: HOW THE NAME ARRIVED, recorded 2026-09-12 from his son: Larry did not recall the name unprompted. His son told him it looked like there was a name on the helmet, and Larry read it off the photograph. So 'Estes' is Larry's reading of the visor lettering, not an independent memory of the man, and it agrees with the machine reading of the same lettering made on 2026-08-09 and magnified on 2026-08-15 (research/people/major-lewis.md). Two readings of one inscription corroborate the lettering, not the wearer: helmets were pooled and swapped. The parts that are memory are what followed the reading: National Guard, called up, and talking to Larry over his shoulder. An Army National Guard aviator on active duty in Vietnam in 1964-65, before any Guard units were mobilized for the war, would be unusual. That is a check to make, not a contradiction: an individual Guardsman could be on active duty, and a man who had been in the Guard before going active would also fit what Larry said. Withdrawal of 'Lewis' for this frame and the open question of who Lewis was: data/people/major-lewis.json.
